_nguon: EN-ALL GĐ 4 (agent A — lá số Tử vi): nhãn giờ, âm dương, quan hệ Mệnh–Cục, Tuần/Triệt, lưu nguyệt, định giờ, thẻ cung, lá số mẫu, cờ an sao. Ban biên tập viết lại từ nghĩa (không dịch sát), {slot} giữ nguyên; chờ người bản xứ duyệt.
tuvi_ls.menh_cuc.binh_hoa: Life and Bureau share one element
tuvi_ls.co.ty_conflict: Born 23:00–23:59: Zi Wei Dou Shu counts this as the Zi hour of the NEXT DAY, while numerology and BaZi here keep the same day. The two parts can be a day apart — that is a convention, not an error.
tuvi_ls.co.nam_phai: Stars are placed with the classic Zi Wei Dou Shu framework; the main stars and the Four Transformations have been checked against several sources, while some Vietnamese-school minor stars still differ between books. Xun and Jie (Void and Cut-off) follow the Vietnamese school, sitting between two palaces, under the tuan_triet key.
tuvi_ls.tt.ghi_chu.npl: This school firmly rejects the idea that the effect spreads to the triad palaces.
tuvi_ls.tt.ghi_chu.vvt: The effect spreads to the triad palaces, and its strength depends on whether the birth year is yin or yang.
tuvi_ls.tt.xung_dot: SETTINGS CONFLICT: the {phai} uses the '{che_do}' range, but the chart is running '{dang}'. {ghi_chu} Resolve this before reading.
tuvi_ls.tt.qua_rong: {so} of 12 palaces fall within Xun/Jie range — at this level the rule can hardly tell palaces apart. Give much less weight to any conclusion that rests on Xun/Jie.
tuvi_ls.tt.ty_le_70_30: The 70/30 figure is a relative ratio. The classical texts never define what '100% strength' means, so the ratio CANNOT be verified — use it to rank priorities, not as a measured quantity.
tuvi_ls.ln.uu_tien: 10-year period > year chart > minor yearly limit > monthly chart — the month only adds colour to the picture of the year and the period.
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dau_quan_thai_tue.cach_t: Starting from the annual Tai Sui palace (the palace carrying the branch of the year being read) as the first lunar month, count backwards to your birth month; from that palace, call it the Zi hour and count forwards to your birth hour → the first-month palace (Dou Jun). Each later month moves forward one palace.
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dau_quan_thai_tue.nguon: The Complete Book of Zi Wei Dou Shu (斗君, 正月初一日管事) — the most common method
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dau_quan_tieu_han.ten: Dou Jun from the minor yearly limit
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dau_quan_tieu_han.cach_t: Like Dou Jun, but the count starts from the minor-yearly-limit palace of the year being read instead of the Tai Sui palace.
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dau_quan_tieu_han.nguon: Some Vietnamese Zi Wei books and sites (placing the monthly limit from the minor yearly limit)
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.tieu_han.ten: First month at the minor yearly limit
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.tieu_han.cach_tinh: The minor-yearly-limit palace of the year being read is the first lunar month; later months move forward. A quick, simplified method.
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.tieu_han.nguon: A quick method common in Vietnam
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.luu_nien.ten: First month at the year-chart palace
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.luu_nien.cach_tinh: The year-chart palace (the palace carrying the branch of the year being read) is the first lunar month; later months move forward — birth month and hour are not used.
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.luu_nien.nguon: The 流年命宮順數月 option in Taiwanese / Hong Kong Zi Wei software
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dia_chi_thang.cach_tinh: The palace carrying the month's earthly branch is the month palace: the first month at Yin, the second at Mao… — the same for every chart in a given year; only the stars inside differ.
tuvi_ls.ln.phai.dia_chi_thang.nguon: The 流月地支 option in Taiwanese Zi Wei software

tuvi_ls.dg.ghi_chu.ty_muon: The time you entered falls in the late Zi hour ({khoang}): Zi Wei Dou Shu moves this hour to the next day, so the chart differs from the early Zi hour chart ({khoang_som}) of the same day.
tuvi_ls.dg.ghi_chu.ty_muon_dong_ho: The time you entered falls in the late Zi hour ({khoang} clock time): Zi Wei Dou Shu moves this hour to the next day, so the chart differs from the early Zi hour chart ({khoang_som} clock time) of the same day.
tuvi_ls.dg.ghi_chu.ty_muon_hom_truoc: The time you entered ({dong_ho} clock time) is {lich} in calendar time — the late Zi hour. Zi Wei Dou Shu moves the late Zi hour to the next day, which is exactly the day you entered, so the chart matches the early Zi hour chart ({khoang_som} clock time) of this day.
tuvi_ls.dg.ghi_chu.hom_truoc: In calendar time, the time you entered is {lich}.
tuvi_ls.dg.mot_gio: Only one hour to look at: add the hour before and the hour after to compare charts.
tuvi_ls.dg.giong_nhau: Life palace, Bureau and Body palace are the same across these hours — the differences lie in where the minor stars sit.
tuvi_ls.dg.loi_dan: Pick the years you remember clearly. For each candidate hour, read the questions for each year and mark the ones that match what you lived through. The hour with more matches is the one worth a closer look.
tuvi_ls.dg.luu_y.1: The questions only ask about things you can observe yourself; the system does not choose your birth hour for you.
tuvi_ls.dg.luu_y.2: There are no health questions: the Health palace only asks about your daily rhythm.
tuvi_ls.dg.luu_y.3: The years you choose and your answers are not stored.
tuvi_ls.dg.luu_y.4: If you are still unsure, the birth certificate or what your family remembers is still the best evidence.
